**A compiled graph is valid only under the assumptions used to capture it.** Guards track relevant shapes, dtypes, devices, and Python state. If a guard fails, the system may need another compiled version. Excessive specialization can create repeated compilation overhead. [1](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/torch.compiler_troubleshooting.html)

A Python condition depending on `tensor.sum()` requires a runtime tensor value. Ordinary tracing cannot always represent both branches automatically; it may break the graph or reject full-graph capture. The exact behavior depends on version and backend.

**Preserve semantics when refactoring.** Supported structured control flow such as `torch.cond` may express branches inside a graph when its requirements are met. Replacing a branch with unconditional computation can change costs or side effects, so it is not automatically equivalent.

Inspect graph-break and recompilation diagnostics before tuning kernels. Test both branches and representative dynamic shapes, and separate cold compilation from steady-state timing. A function that is fast after one carefully chosen warmup input may still recompile repeatedly on real traffic. Compilation is useful when the captured workload matches deployment.

**Technical details and references.**

Torch compilation specializes captured graphs under guards about shapes, dtypes, devices, and relevant Python state. A failed guard can trigger recompilation. Data-dependent Python branching such as `if tensor.sum() > 0` requires a runtime tensor value, so ordinary tracing may produce a graph break or raise an error under full-graph capture rather than representing both branches automatically. [1](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/torch.compiler_troubleshooting.html)

Use supported structured control flow such as `torch.cond` where appropriate, or refactor the computation while preserving semantics. Diagnose graph breaks, guard failures, and recompilation counts before optimizing kernels. A graph break can fall back to eager execution and then resume compiled segments, losing fusion and adding overhead. Behavior is version/backend dependent, so inspect diagnostics for the installed version and test both branches and dynamic shapes, not just one warmup input.
